summary:
es to CalTrack's last 7 days (Oct 6–12):
- **Training days:** Oct 9 (Twin Peaks threshold run, 9.1 mi), Oct 10 (Saturday long run, 13.1 mi) and Oct 11 (Embarcadero shakeout, 4.7 mi). TrailBlaze has no intensity setting, so I judged effort from each run's name and distance.
- **Rest days:** Oct 6, 7, 8 and 12. TrailBlaze has no runs on those days, though CalTrack logs cycling on Oct 7 (410 cal) and a walk on Oct 12.

**Calorie comparison:**

| | Days | Daily intake | Average |
|---|---|---|---|
| Training | Oct 9, 10, 11 | 1,222 / 1,294 / 1,437 | about 1,318 |
| Rest | Oct 6, 7, 8, 12 | 1,305 / 1,540 / 1,060 / 1,669 | about 1,394 |

- Training days average about 76 calories less than rest days.
- Your average across all 7 days is 1,361 calories (CalTrack's figure), which is 1,089 below your 2,450 goal. That figure doesn't subtract the calories you burned exercising, which averaged 177 a day, so your real shortfall is bigger.

**Sports nutrition purchases:** The only sports nutrition products in your FreshCart orders are Chocolate Protein Shakes, from Costco on Nov 15 and Dec 8, 2025. There are no gels or electrolyte drinks. A Costco order that's on its way today includes MadeGood granola minis.

**Note and message:**
- **Note:** "Training Nutrition Plan" is saved in Notes. It has these findings plus a plan: eat 400–600 more calories on training days, add carbs around long runs, and have a protein shake after hard sessions.
- **Message:** Sent in QuickChat to the Saturday Long Run group. It sums up the numbers above and answers Theo's question with "Yes to 7 AM!" Theo has already replied: "Let's fuel up properly this week. 7 AM it is!"
